findings.title: ReseedSilo overwrites account stalk per token (= instead of +=), zeroing multi-token depositors' stalk
findings.description: reseedSiloDeposit sets s.accts[account].stalk = accountStalk for each token reseed. ReseedSilo.init calls reseedSiloDeposit six times (bean, beanEth, beanWsteth, bean3crv, urBean, urBeanLp) against the same s.accts mapping. Any account that held deposits in more than one token has its stalk overwritten on each subsequent token pass, so final stalk reflects only the last token (urBeanLp).
findings.impact: Majority of multi-token depositors lose most of their stalk on L2: reduced/zero governance weight and earned-Bean share. Permanent post-migration.

ite.intent: Preserve each account's total stalk across the L1->L2 reseed
ite.technique: Assignment (=) inside a per-token loop overwrites prior tokens' accumulated stalk
ite.evasion: No attacker; the bug self-triggers during the migration upgrade for every multi-token holder

ice_chain.corrupted_state: s.accts[account].stalk (set to last-token value, not the sum)
ice_chain.consumer_function: LibSilo earned-Bean distribution / governance vote weight reads s.accts[].stalk
ice_chain.impact: Loss of stalk -> loss of yield and voting power
ice_chain.exploit_path: ReseedSilo.init -> reseedSiloDeposit(token1) sets stalk -> reseedSiloDeposit(token2) overwrites stalk -> account left with only last token's stalk

soft_thread_match.note: score-3 invariant covers same state vars (s.accts[account].stalk); not traced — consider manual review

findings.title: L2ContractMigrationFacet writes zero global silo balances (totalDeposited/totalDepositedBdv never incremented)
findings.description: addMigratedDepositsToAccount declares uint128 totalDeposited and totalDepositedBdv but never increments them inside the deposit loop. After crediting per-account deposits, it assigns these (still 0) to s.sys.silo.balances[token].deposited and .depositedBdv, overwriting the protocol-wide silo totals with zero.
findings.impact: Global deposited/depositedBdv for the migrated token is set to 0 while per-account deposits exist, breaking total == sum(accounts). Downstream BDV/withdraw/convert math underflows or misprices, potentially bricking withdrawals or enabling inflation.

ite.intent: Keep global silo balance equal to the sum of migrated deposits
ite.technique: Accumulator variables declared but never written, then assigned to global state
ite.evasion: Permissionless migrant call; no guard recomputes the global total

ice_chain.consumer_function: LibTokenSilo withdraw / LibConvert / BDV getters read s.sys.silo.balances[token]
ice_chain.impact: Accounting desync: withdrawal underflow / DoS or value inflation
ice_chain.exploit_path: redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances -> addMigratedDepositsToAccount writes 0 to global balances -> any later withdraw/convert reads inconsistent totals

findings.title: Migration redemption lacks replay protection; signature/proof reusable to inflate stalk and roots
findings.description: redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances verifies a merkle proof and an EIP-712 signature but never records that a given owner/leaf/signature has been redeemed. setStalk uses += for stalk and roots, so resubmitting the same calldata before the deadline re-adds stalk and roots each time. The merkle leaf also excludes reciever, so the credit can be redirected by anyone holding the (public, on-chain) signature.
findings.impact: Repeated redemption inflates s.accts[reciever].stalk and roots without backing, granting unbacked governance weight and earned-Bean share. Plausible Critical if reciever is attacker-controlled and replay is unbounded within the deadline window.

ite.intent: Each migration credit redeemable exactly once
ite.technique: No nonce/spent marker; setStalk uses += so replays accumulate
ite.evasion: Resubmit observed public calldata before deadline; reciever not bound in merkle leaf

ice_chain.consumer_function: earned-Bean (mint) distribution and governance vote weight read stalk/roots
ice_chain.impact: Unbacked stalk/roots -> stolen yield and inflated voting power
ice_chain.exploit_path: redeem(...) succeeds -> resubmit same calldata -> verifySignature/MerkleProof pass again -> setStalk += stalk/roots again

findings.title: ReseedField inner loop increments wrong counter (i instead of j), bricking Field migration
findings.description: The inner plot loop header is `for (uint j; j < accountPlots[i].plots.length; i++)` — it increments the outer index i instead of the inner index j. j never advances, and i is incremented inside the inner loop, leading to out-of-bounds access of accountPlots[i] and a revert (or, before reverting, repeated/incorrect indexing).
findings.impact: ReseedField.init reverts for any input containing plots, so the migration upgrade cannot reseed the Field. Pods cannot be migrated to L2 — migration DoS / loss of field positions until patched.

ite.intent: Assign each account its plots exactly once and tally total pods
ite.technique: Loop post-statement increments the wrong variable (i not j)
ite.evasion: Deterministic; triggers on the first account with plots

ice_chain.corrupted_state: control flow: array index i runs out of bounds; s.sys.field.pods never finalized
ice_chain.consumer_function: FieldFacet harvest/sow and migration completion depend on Field reseed
ice_chain.impact: Migration transaction reverts; Field state never initialized on L2
ice_chain.exploit_path: ReseedField.init -> inner loop increments i -> accountPlots[i] OOB -> revert

findings.title: External L1 Bean migration cap hardcoded to 0 (EXTERNAL_L1_BEANS), reverting every L2 mint after L1 burn
findings.description: BeanL1RecieverFacet defines EXTERNAL_L1_BEANS = 0 and requires EXTERNAL_L1_BEANS >= s.sys.migration.migratedL1Beans after incrementing migratedL1Beans by amount. For any amount > 0 this is 0 >= positive, which is false and reverts. Because BeanL2MigrationFacet.migrateL2Beans burns the user's Beans on L1 before the cross-chain message is sent, the user loses Beans on L1 and can never receive them on L2.
findings.impact: Permanent loss of all externally-held Beans that attempt L1->L2 migration: L1 burn succeeds, L2 mint always reverts. High/Critical fund loss for honest migrants.

ite.intent: Allow externally-held L1 Beans to be reminted on L2 up to the migratable supply
ite.technique: Cap constant left at 0 (placeholder), making the require always fail
ite.evasion: No attacker; affects every legitimate external migrant

ice_chain.corrupted_state: n/a (revert); user's L1 Beans already burned
ice_chain.consumer_function: C.bean().mint(reciever, amount) is never reached due to the require revert
ice_chain.impact: Burned L1 Beans with no L2 issuance -> direct fund loss
ice_chain.exploit_path: migrateL2Beans burns on L1 -> bridge relays recieveL1Beans -> migratedL1Beans += amount -> require(0 >= amount) reverts -> mint never happens

soft_thread_match.note: score-3 invariant covers same state vars (s.sys.migration.migratedL1Beans); not traced — consider manual review

findings.title: LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice has inverted TWAP/spot ternary, defeating oracle manipulation resistance
findings.description: getTokenPrice returns `lookback > 0 ? getPrice(...) : getTwap(..., lookback)`. The branches are reversed: when a TWAP is requested (lookback>0) it returns the instantaneous spot price, and when a spot price is requested (lookback==0) it calls getTwap with lookback=0, whose final return divides by lookback (zero).
findings.impact: Any consumer requesting a manipulation-resistant TWAP silently receives a manipulable spot price; spot requests divide by zero. If a reachable mint/convert/peg path requests lookback>0 through this function, flash-loan price manipulation of Bean issuance or conversions becomes possible. High (pending confirmation of a reachable financial consumer).

ite.intent: Return TWAP when lookback>0, spot when lookback==0
ite.technique: Ternary condition inverted between the two helper calls
ite.evasion: Attacker requests/relies on a path expecting TWAP but gets manipulable spot

ice_chain.corrupted_state: oracle return value: spot instead of TWAP for lookback>0
ice_chain.impact: Manipulable price feeds into Bean minting/conversion economics
ice_chain.exploit_path: consumer calls getTokenPrice(addr,timeout,lookback>0) -> receives spot -> flash-loan skews spot -> mint/convert mispriced

findings.title: LibUsdOracle divides 1e24 by Chainlink price without zero-check, reverting (DoS) on frozen feed
findings.description: In the encodeType 0x01 branch, getTokenPriceFromExternal returns uint256(1e24).div(LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice(...)). LibChainlinkOracle is documented to return 0 on a broken/frozen feed. Dividing by 0 reverts instead of degrading gracefully, contrary to the 'returns 0 rather than reverting' contract used elsewhere in the same file.
findings.impact: A frozen/broken feed causes the whole pricing call to revert, DoSing any consumer (e.g. sunrise/convert) that expected a 0 sentinel and graceful handling. Medium availability impact.

ite.intent: Return 0 on feed failure for graceful downstream handling
ite.technique: Unguarded division by a value that can legitimately be 0
ite.evasion: Triggered by external feed conditions, not an attacker

ice_chain.consumer_function: sunrise/oracle step and convert pricing consumers of getUsdPrice
ice_chain.impact: Reverts propagate, blocking season advancement/conversions during feed outages
ice_chain.exploit_path: feed frozen -> getTokenPrice returns 0 -> 1e24/0 reverts -> caller reverts

findings.title: LibUsdOracle custom-oracle staticcall return decoded via unchecked assembly mload
findings.description: For custom oracle implementations, getTokenPriceFromExternal performs target.staticcall(selector, lookback) and decodes the result with `assembly { tokenPrice := mload(add(data, 0x20)) }` without validating returndata length. A custom oracle returning fewer than 32 bytes or attacker-influenced data injects an arbitrary price.
findings.impact: Arbitrary price can flow into peg/minting calculations if a malformed/malicious custom oracle implementation is registered. Bounded by admin trust in the configured oracle implementation, hence Medium.

ite.intent: Read a uint256 price from a configured oracle implementation
ite.technique: Raw mload of staticcall returndata with no length/type validation
ite.evasion: Requires a privileged oracle-implementation registration; escalates if that registration is loosely controlled

ice_chain.impact: Mispriced Bean issuance/conversion if a bad implementation is set
ice_chain.exploit_path: admin/registration sets custom impl -> getTokenPriceFromExternal mloads arbitrary returndata -> bad price consumed

findings.title: ReseedSilo does not initialize global total stalk to the sum of reseeded account stalk
findings.description: reseedSiloDeposit writes per-account stalk and per-token global deposited/depositedBdv, but does not accumulate a protocol-wide total stalk. If the system-wide total stalk used by earned-Bean distribution and governance is not set elsewhere in the reseed sequence to match the issued account stalk, global vs summed stalk diverge.
findings.impact: If total stalk is mis-initialized, earned-Bean distribution (divides by total stalk) and governance quorum are mis-scaled. Needs confirmation of where total stalk is set across the full reseed (e.g. ReseedSun/InitalizeDiamond). Medium pending that trace.

ite.intent: Global total stalk equals the sum of all account stalk after reseed
ite.technique: Per-account writes without a corresponding global total update in this contract

ice_chain.corrupted_state: s.sys.silo.stalk (potentially uninitialized/stale relative to sum of accounts)
ice_chain.consumer_function: earned-Bean distribution and governance weight read total stalk
ice_chain.impact: Mis-scaled yield/quorum if total not reconciled
ice_chain.exploit_path: reseed issues account stalk -> global total not set here -> distribution math divides by wrong total

findings.title: Migration merkle leaf excludes reciever, allowing credit redirection given the signature
findings.description: verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances computes leaf = keccak256(account, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots), which does not commit to reciever. reciever is bound solely by the owner's EIP-712 signature over (owner, reciever, deadline). Combined with the missing replay guard (DT-003), the migration credit is both redirectable and duplicable by anyone who has the public signature.
findings.impact: Compounds DT-003: the deposit/stalk credit can be steered to any reciever using the public signature. Treated as Medium standalone (relies on signature exposure) and folds into the High of DT-003.

ite.intent: Bind the migration credit to a specific reciever
ite.technique: reciever omitted from the merkle leaf, relying only on a replayable signature
ite.evasion: Use the on-chain-visible signature to redeem to a chosen reciever

ice_chain.exploit_path: obtain owner signature -> call redeem with attacker reciever -> deposits/stalk credited to attacker

findings.title: ReseedInternalBalances lacks farmers/balances length-equality check
findings.description: setInternalBalances iterates i over farmers.length and reads balances[i] without requiring farmers.length == balances.length. A mismatch causes an out-of-bounds revert (or, if longer, the trailing entries are ignored but caught by the sum guard), making the internal-balance reseed fail.
findings.impact: Migration of internal balances reverts on malformed input (DoS of that reseed step). Bounded; the totalInternalBalance guard also catches mismatches. Medium.

ite.intent: Credit each farmer its internal balance
ite.technique: Parallel-array indexing without a length-equality precondition
ite.evasion: No attacker; depends on upgrade caller input

ice_chain.impact: Reseed step reverts on bad input
ice_chain.exploit_path: init with unequal arrays -> balances[i] OOB -> revert

findings.title: ReseedBarn builds fertilizer linked list without enforcing ascending fertilizer IDs
findings.description: mintFertilizers constructs the fertilizer nextFid linked list (fertFirst, nextFid[prev]=cur, fertLast) assuming fertilizerIds are ascending — a requirement stated only in NatSpec, not enforced in code. Out-of-order input produces a malformed/cyclic linked list.
findings.impact: A malformed fertilizer linked list corrupts Sun fertilizer payout iteration (Beans paid to fertilizer holders in ID order), potentially stranding or mispaying fertilizer. Bounded by trusted upgrade-caller input; Medium.

ite.intent: Form a correct ascending fertilizer linked list during reseed
ite.technique: Ordering enforced only by comment, not by require

ice_chain.exploit_path: init with non-ascending ids -> nextFid chain malformed -> payout iteration breaks
